title: How to Play Rummy with 2, 3 or 4 Players: Cards, Decks and Setup
excerpt: How many cards to deal and how many decks to use for 2, 3, 4 or more players, in both classic rummy and 13-card Indian rummy.
content:
**Short answer:** it depends on which rummy you are playing. In **classic rummy**, deal 10 cards each for 2 players, 7 each for 3 or 4 players, and 6 each for 5 or 6 players, from one deck. In **13-card Indian rummy**, everyone gets 13 cards, and games with 3 or more players normally use two decks plus jokers.

This guide explains card-game rules for general knowledge. Online rummy played for money is prohibited in India under the Online Gaming Act, 2025; see our [online gaming laws guide](/blog/online-gaming-laws-in-india-what-players-should-know). 18+ only.

## Quick Setup Table

| Players | Classic rummy (one 52-card deck) | 13-card Indian rummy |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 10 cards each | 13 cards each, one or two decks |
| 3 | 7 cards each | 13 cards each, two decks |
| 4 | 7 cards each | 13 cards each, two decks |
| 5 to 6 | 6 cards each | 13 cards each, two decks |

These are the common conventions; house rules vary.

## Classic Rummy: How to Play

Classic rummy is the widely played Western version.

- **Deal:** shuffle one deck and deal the number of cards shown above, one at a time. Turn the next card face up to start the discard pile; the rest is the stock.
- **Your turn:** draw the top card of the stock or the discard pile, then discard one card.
- **Melds:** lay down sets (3 or 4 cards of the same rank) or runs (3 or more consecutive cards of the same suit) on your turn. You can also add single cards to melds already on the table ("laying off").
- **Going out:** the first player to meld or lay off all their cards wins the hand.
- **Scoring:** the winner scores the value of the cards left in everyone else's hands, commonly face cards 10, Aces 1 and number cards their face value.

## 13-Card Indian Rummy: How Player Count Changes the Game

In Indian rummy the hand size stays at 13 whatever the number of players. What changes is the deck count and the pace:

- **2 players:** faster, more focused games; you can often track exactly what your opponent is collecting.
- **3 or 4 players:** two decks are used, so duplicate cards appear. Remember that a set still cannot contain two cards of the same suit.
- **5 or 6 players:** the closed pile runs down faster, so building your pure sequence early matters even more.

The full rules, including jokers and the pure sequence requirement, are in [how to play 13-card rummy](/blog/how-to-play-13-card-rummy-rules).

## Tips for Two-Player Rummy

- Watch every card your opponent picks from the discard pile. With only one opponent, it shows exactly what they need.
- Avoid discarding cards next to ones they have just picked up.
- In classic rummy, holding cards too long can cost you. Laying down melds early reduces your points if your opponent goes out.

## Tips for Three and Four Players

- Discards reveal less, because several players are collecting at once.
- In 13-card rummy, discard high-value cards you cannot use early, to limit your points if someone else declares.
- Agree on the scoring and drop rules before the first deal.

For more on scoring, see [rummy points calculation](/blog/rummy-points-calculation), and for knowing when to fold a bad hand, [when to drop in rummy](/blog/when-to-drop-in-rummy).
